  "text": "The footsteps stopped at the top of the stairs.

“Keeper?” the harbor master called.

A knock came through the pipe instead: twice, then once. Mara’s father lifted the lantern. Scratched into the brass beside the mouthpiece were three small marks in the same pattern.

“That isn’t an answer,” he said.

The footsteps began again, slower now. Mara watched the gauge. Its needle held steady below the red band, but the glass pane beyond the stone door had gone dark. Whatever had pressed its hand against it was gone.

The keeper appeared on the stairs carrying a coil of rope. Water streamed from his sleeves. Behind him came a woman in a ship’s coat, one arm braced against the wall.

“Found her in the lower passage,” he said. “The gate was holding the water back from the harbor, but it was flooding everything on this side.”

The woman squinted at the plate beneath the QUAY wheel. “Who painted over that?”

“No one knows,” the harbor master said.

“I do.” She pointed to the black flakes at Mara’s feet. “That paint is fresh. I saw a man carrying a tin of it onto the quay this morning.”

A bell rang overhead. Once, then twice.

The keeper’s face changed. “That’s the warning from the outer buoy.”

“For what?” Mara asked.

He crossed to the dark pane and held the lantern against it. Far beyond the glass, a row of lights was moving through the water toward the lighthouse.

“Ships,” said Mara’s father.

The keeper shook his head. “Ships don’t travel beneath the harbor.”"
